### Claude PR Review

- [x] Read changed files
- [x] Analyze against repo conventions
- [x] Post review

Overall the change is a clean, well-motivated refactor: correct use of the module boundary (route service goes through the new `IZerionRepository` instead of reaching into another module's datasource), single portfolio fetch per environment, and thoughtful degrade paths. Below are things worth improving before merge — all minor.

#### Nits / suggestions

**1. `Map<boolean, ...>` is a slightly clumsy key** — `src/modules/safe/routes/v2/safes.v2.service.ts:214`

```ts
const networksByEnvironment = new Map<boolean, Record<string, string>>();
```

Only two possible values ever exist. A plain object `{ mainnet, testnet }` (or two named locals) would read more clearly and remove the `[...new Set(chains.map(c => c.isTestnet))]` dance below it. Not a bug — readability only.

**2. Zerion chain list is fetched even when no request chain uses that environment** — `src/modules/safe/routes/v2/safes.v2.service.ts:215-234`

`resolveZerionChainNames` fans out on `[...new Set(chains.map(c => c.isTestnet))]`, which is correct today. Fine as-is, but note that a request containing only unresolved chains (`chain === null` for all entries) will short-circuit before the fetch — that's already handled by the `.filter((c): c is Chain => c !== null)` on line 211. Good.

**3. `resolveZerionChainNames` warn payload uses `LogType.PortfolioRequestError`** — `src/modules/safe/routes/v2/safes.v2.service.ts:225`

The failing call is not a portfolio request — it's the chain-list request. Reusing `PortfolioRequestError` here will make dashboards over that LogType noisy with a different failure class. Consider a distinct log type (e.g. `ZerionChainListError`) so degradation caused by the chain-list lookup is separable from actual portfolio failures.

**4. Log severity change in the mapping service is intentional but subtle** — `src/modules/zerion/datasources/zerion-chain-mapping.service.ts:82`

Dropping the unknown-chain-ID log from `warn` to `debug` is correct given the overview now probes every chain, but the same helper is still called by `getNetworkFromChainId` from the positions path — every unknown chain there also loses its warning. If the positions endpoint relies on that warning to surface config drift, it silently goes away. Worth confirming that isn't a regression the follow-up you mention will need to re-add.

**5. `ZerionRepository` is a one-line pass-through** — `src/modules/zerion/domain/zerion.repository.ts:12-18`

It exists to satisfy the module-boundary rule (route services import via `domain/`), which is fine and correct. The rename `getChainIdToNetworkMapping` → `getNetworksByChainId` slightly obscures the shape: the returned map is keyed by chainId and the value is a network name (singular). `getNetworkByChainId` (or `getNetworkNameByChainId`) matches the return shape better.

**6. Docstrings on the new private helpers are on the longer side** — `src/modules/safe/routes/v2/safes.v2.service.ts:138-142, 171-175, 196-203, 244-249, 301-306, 386-390, 402-406, 436-439`

`cgw-best-practices` prefers no comments unless the WHY is non-obvious. Several of these describe WHAT (`Resolves each unique chainId once`, `Fetches one portfolio per unique wallet-identity`) which the method name already conveys; the WHY parts (why validate-first, why per-identity) are the parts worth keeping.

**7. Test coverage looks solid** — unit spec covers Zerion-listed vs. not, both-environment split, Zerion chain lookup failure, and the absent-from-distribution real-zero. Integration spec includes chain-list-request-failure. No visible gap.

Nothing here blocks merge; item 3 (log type) and item 4 (dropped warning) are the two worth a second look before shipping.
